text: You seem to have lost the context when I closed the "TicTacToe" folder and opened the current "AGI-experiment" folder.  Anyway, I looked at the current file and I wonder if layer 1 and layer 2 as suggested by you are redundant?  What justifies to have these 2 layers?  Thanks for your hard work so far.

This seems to touch on the question whether we should have a "long-term memory" module, and how might LTM and WM work together.  The system may learn about a French general as general_1, and later learn that his name is Napoleon.  This entity may become more like a "constant."  How can we handle these situations elegantly?

Thanks for the solution proposal, it looks reasonable and promising.  It also brings up another idea that, since we have the logic structure, the training of this "LLM" or "AGI" might be accelerated by utilizing some logical pre-processing akin to natural-language processing.  This is not the case with the training of traditional LLM models.  Moreover, we seem to not have explicated the interaction between LTM and WM.  Would the LTM be some kind of content-addressible memory?

Great!  
1) Let's break down the .md files to make them more organized with specific topics.
2) What size text corpus should we prepare for a first experiment?
The latest outline of "steps for implementation" looks good!
One more question for my understanding, before we proceed:   in entities management, option C: attention-based resolution, is this attention network separate from our neural logic network?

For the "concepts" outputted by self.logic_rules, I suppose they have their positions within the proposition, right?  Also, we seem to lack a .md file explaining the LogicNetwork.  Shall we copy one from the TTT repo?

Now I see the concepts are like triplets, but how does a triple get compared (similarity) to entities?  For example, if the concept is "Napoleon born_in Corsica," then it could potentially give attention to "Napoleon", "born in", or "Corsica".  How does that work exactly?
What if the concept needs to generate a constant as subject, object, or relation?  Is that doable?
For entities, your examples used tags like "is_a" and "Napoleon", are these tags for illustrative purpose only, or is there a way to learn them?
But if we keep the NL tags for entities, does that enable us to examine the logic network's internal propositions?  More or less in human-readable form?

I have run experiments on another machine -- it passed phase 1 & 2 tests with excellence.  I want to draw a better "string diagram" for the neural logic network (category-theory style).  This time I want to use more compact symbols and use small-font numbers to mark the diagram and explain the tags with paragraphs under the diagram.   I have made one such diagram, ./string-diagram2.svg, but you don't have to copy the style exactly.  Also don't mind about the size of the canvas / paper.  If possible, make the paths editable so that I can modify them on Inkscape.
Looking at the diagram, isn't it strange that relation selection does not depend on the subject selected?  And object selection does not depend on the subject and relation selected?
Perhaps I read the diagram wrong?  but I understand the information flow is from top to bottom.  Oh!  I see now... those dotted arrows are feedback arrows moving information upwards...
